items.prompt: Explain how government and a consumer group can address Nela’s misleading product information. Fictional Nela Goods advertises a feature its product does not provide. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Consumers can be disadvantaged by unsafe goods, misleading claims, poor information or unfair treatment. Government can support accurate information, suitable product standards, complaint routes and enforcement. Consumer pressure groups can test products, share reliable comparisons, publicise concerns and encourage better conduct. A pressure group can influence reputation and purchasing but does not automatically have a regulator’s enforcement power. Measures need evidence, access and implementation; an inaccurate accusation can mislead buyers too. Identify the consumer relationship rather than substitute employee pay or lender security. Accurate correction and a credible complaint route address buyers’ information problem. An independent consumer comparison can inform choice, while enforcement can address the misleading conduct. A worker bonus would not correct the customer claim.

items.prompt: Explain why truthful reporting and agreed collateral matter to Omi’s finance provider. Fictional Omi Tools seeks finance using inaccurate financial records. It also offers an asset as collateral. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Lenders and investors need reliable information about a business and the terms on which funds are supplied. Government can support truthful reporting, action against fraud and appropriate enforcement of financial agreements. A lender may also use agreed collateral: an asset securing repayment if the borrower defaults, subject to the arrangement. This is loan security, not a guard outside the building. Limited liability normally protects owners’ exposure, not the lender from loss. Protection can reduce deception and improve informed decisions but cannot remove ordinary commercial risk or guarantee repayment and investment returns. Truthful records help a provider assess cash, debt and risk; collateral may reduce loss if valid and sufficient. Neither a security guard nor a profit claim guarantees repayment.

items.prompt: Explain the relevant meaning of security when fictional Eha Repairs pledges equipment for a loan and also employs a gate guard. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The pledged equipment is loan security or collateral, potentially supporting recovery if repayment fails under the agreement. The guard provides physical security. Guarding the gate does not give the lender the same repayment claim or eliminate credit risk.

items.prompt: Evaluate whether accurate information with investigation and follow-up suits Tula better than a general publicity slogan. Fictional Tula Goods misstates a product feature to buyers and separately supplies unreliable accounts to a lender. [8]
items.canonical_answer: Evaluate protection by identifying who faces which risk, how a measure addresses it and what implementation costs or limits remain. Product claims concern consumers; disclosure and financial agreements concern capital providers. One business can require both protections, and a measure useful for one risk may leave another untouched. Information can improve choice, while persistent deceptive conduct may require investigation and enforcement. The discussion is conceptual rather than a judgement about a current legal case. Correct product information addresses buyers; verified financial disclosure addresses the lender. Prefer proportionate investigation and follow-up on both issues rather than a publicity slogan alone, while recognising administrative cost and residual business risk.

items.prompt:
Fictional Hela Goods makes a misleading product claim and supplies inaccurate accounts when seeking a loan. A consumer group can publish a checked comparison. A hypothetical regulator can investigate the claims and reporting. Management proposes a general trust-us poster instead.

a(i) State two mechanisms protecting consumers. [2]
a(ii) State two criteria for evaluating a protection measure. [2]
b State two interests consumers need protected when buying. [2]
c Explain why Hela’s lender needs truthful accounts rather than a physical security guard. [6]
d Evaluate verified correction and investigation against the poster alone. [8]
items.canonical_answer: a(i) Accurate product information and a credible complaint route. a(ii) Whether it addresses the stated risk and whether it is implemented. b Safe suitable products and truthful claims. c Accounts support assessment of repayment cash, debts and risk; a guard protects premises but does not verify the borrower’s position or establish collateral rights. d A checked correction and investigation target the two forms of misleading information. The poster communicates reassurance without supplying missing evidence. Prefer the targeted response, while recognising its cost and that truthful records still do not guarantee repayment.

items.prompt:
Fictional Hela Goods makes a misleading product claim and supplies inaccurate accounts when seeking a loan. A consumer group can publish a checked comparison. A hypothetical regulator can investigate the claims and reporting. Management proposes a general trust-us poster instead.

a Explain how Hela’s consumers and capital provider face different information risks. [8]
b Evaluate the consumer group’s role compared with the regulator’s role in responding. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a Buyers need an accurate product description for choice and use; the lender needs accurate financial evidence for repayment assessment. One correction cannot automatically satisfy both. A checked product comparison helps buyers but does not establish the firm’s cash position. b The group can inform consumers and create reputational pressure, but its findings need accuracy and it lacks assumed regulatory enforcement powers. The regulator can investigate under the stated hypothetical authority and require appropriate follow-up. Use both complementary roles: reliable public information and proportionate investigation of persistent conduct. Neither should be presented as removing every commercial risk.

items.prompt:
Fictional Nara Tools has incorrect product information and unclear financial disclosures. Verified corrections and accessible complaint handling can address both; management compares that approach with publicity alone.

Evaluate verified correction and complaint handling against publicity alone at Nara. Give a concise plan. [12]
items.canonical_answer: Identify groups: buyers need product truth; capital providers need financial disclosure. Correction addresses actual inaccuracies; complaint handling reveals unresolved effects. Publicity alone may repeat reassurance without evidence. Costs include checking and administration. Judgement: prefer verified correction with follow-up, recognising ordinary business risk remains and different records serve different users.

items.prompt:
Fictional Nara Tools has incorrect product information and unclear financial disclosures. Verified corrections and accessible complaint handling can address both; management compares that approach with publicity alone. For part (b) only, management refuses correction and continues the same misleading conduct after complaints. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate the corrective approach at Nara under the original facts. [12]
b Evaluate the response after management refuses correction. Explain whether the earlier approach remains sufficient. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a Verified corrections and accessible complaints address the stated information failures more directly than publicity. Check that buyers and finance providers receive the relevant corrected evidence, and monitor recurrence. b Refusal and continued misleading conduct show voluntary correction is insufficient. Escalate to appropriate investigation and enforcement under the stated protective arrangements, while consumer groups can provide checked information. The objective remains accurate information, but the response must change because cooperation and implementation have failed. Do not promise that enforcement guarantees every investment return.
